title: AI model for urine cytology whole-slide images detects urothelial carcinoma
summary: The Precision Urine Cytology AI Solution (PUCAS) was trained on 2,641 patients and validated retrospectively in 2,335 patients and prospectively in 400 patients across four Chinese hospitals. Sensitivity ranged from 0.922 to 1.000 in retrospective cohorts and was 0.896 (95% CI 0.837-0.939) prospectively. In the recurrence-detection scenario it could reduce endoscopy use by 57.5% with a negative predictive value of 96.4%, and validation in other countries is still needed.
ai_technology: Whole-slide-image deep-learning pipeline (patch extraction, feature extraction, classification) for urine cytology
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hospital

evidence.tested: Diagnostic sensitivity was validated in retrospective and prospective cohorts against histopathology.
evidence.unknown: Performance outside China and effect on patient care are unknown. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning classifier read scanned liquid-based cytology slides to diagnose urothelial carcinoma.
